items.body_excerpt:
Staggs playing for pride, culture and for fitting farewells
With a sold out crowd expected and playing for pride in his jersey and for his culture, Broncos leader Kotoni Staggs said motivation was high to face the Warriors.
A proud Wiradjuri man, Staggs said playing at home at Suncorp Stadium for Indigenous Round added a special layer of meaning to play well - not just for himself but for his community.
“I love taking part in these games and they're very special to myself because I'm not only representing myself, I'm representing my family and my community as well back home," Staggs said.
Kotoni Staggs with the Deadly Choices Indigenous Round training shirt. ©Brisbane Broncos
“I always stand proud and stand tall for who I am and where I come from.
“I carry that with me no matter where I go, I'll make sure that people know that I am a very proud Indigenous man, a Wiradjuri boy as well and I'm always proud of where I come from and who I am as well.”
Kotoni Staggs and Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow exchange Aboriginal and Torres Strait Island gifts before last week's Indigenous Round match between the Dolphins and the Broncos. ©Scott Davis / NRL Images
As well as being part of this special round, Staggs said despite it being a “frustrating” season where they could not mount a title defence following last year's stunning premiership victory, the squad were working hard to send out some club legends as winners.
Representative forward Payne Haas is leaving to rejoin Wayne Bennett at the Rabbitohs while captain Adam Reynolds, who is set to miss a number of weeks with a calf injury suffered at training this week, is hanging up the boots.
Kotoni Staggs and Adam Reynolds celebrate the 2025 grand final win. ©NRL Images
“We look at our games, what we could have done here, what we could have done there,” Staggs said of being out of finals contention.
“It's very sad not getting to where we wanted to get to in the finals again and chasing another trophy.
“But at the end of the day, we've got four more games left and we've got players that aren’t going to be with us next year and we want to send them off on a high.
“Reyno’s retiring, Payne's leaving and what Payne's done for this club, he deserves to be sent off with a few wins under his belt, so we're going to do everything we can to get the wins for them.
“We're still not going to give up, we've got things to play for and we'd love to be playing for another grand final, but we've still got other things to do.”
Coach Michael Maguire said the side were looking forward to the occasion ahead, with many of his younger players also set to give a glimpse into the club’s future next year.
Related Match Preview
Broncos v Warriors: Duffy ready to grow; Metcalf's central role
In the absence of Reynolds, Tom Duffy is partnering Ezra Mam in the halves, while rising forward Va'a (VJ) Semu gets another opportunity from the bench the impress.
“They've been upbeat and ripping in training," Maguire said.
“Obviously, they know the task that's in front of us and we're playing against a high-quality team, so the boys are looking forward to a really good clash.
“Tommy's jumped in. I've said that earlier in many of these press conferences that I've been really impressed with Tommy.
“He grabs the team, he knows what he wants, so I'm really looking forward to him growing each game that he plays.
Va'a Semu in action against the Dolphins. ©Zain Mohammed / NRL Images
“Every time I see him train with the group, he's getting better and better, so looking forward to having that into the future and obviously VJ, he's growing in himself as well.
“When you're in the middle of the park, it's a pretty tough position to play.
“You learn things and he's obviously got people like Payne and Patty and those guys around to be able to learn from.”

NRL Casualty Ward: Fresh Reynolds injury; Ramien's season over
Broncos veteran Adam Reynolds faces a battle to return to the field before hanging up the boots after suffering a calf strain at training on Wednesday.
The premiership winner has not played since suffering a head knock in the Round 22 loss to the Knights and the latest setback puts his hopes of playing out his final season before retiring at the end of the year at risk.
In a statement, the Broncos said Reynolds will be assessed on a weekly basis to determine a return to play.
"Scans at the Clive Berghofer Centre’s Qscan facility confirmed that Broncos captain Adam Reynolds sustained a grade 1 soleus strain on his right calf at training yesterday," the club said.
"His return-to-play timeline will be determined on a week-by-week basis."
Cronulla centre Jesse Ramien has also played his final game for the club with the centre undergoing season-ending pectoral surgery on Thursday.
Ramien suffered the injury in the second half of last week's loss to St George Illawarra and will depart the Sharks at the end of the season to join the Cowboys.
"A big blow for the Sharks with Jesse Ramien ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season after undergoing pectoral repair surgery today," the club said in a statement.
"The star centre hurt himself in the second half against the Dragons on Sunday afternoon; he then went for scans on Monday, but after seeing a specialist, it was decided the best course of action was surgery."

A team of two halves
Fans would’ve hope that the Broncos could repeat their first half effort against the Dolphins in Round 23 which saw them score 5 tries in thrilling fashion. With just 46% possession and a 79% completion rate, they couldn’t turn their 9.6m per carry into more points. While they set a strong platform in attack, they were loose defensively, allowing 7 line breaks and missing 27 tackles. Ultimately, the power of their opponents was too much. Quality and execution to determine the winner
The Broncos have been flattered with the odds that are posted, and the value immediately rests with the Warriors. There is no doubt that they will be motivated ahead of this contest but the relentless pressure the Warriors build in their play should expose the lack of maturity the Broncos possess.

Broncos v Warriors: Duffy ready to grow; Metcalf's central role
The Warriors will continue their pursuit of the minor premiership when they travel to Brisbane to face the Broncos on Saturday night.
Wahs Fever took over Suncorp Stadium when the two sides clashed during Magic Round earlier this season and similar scenes are expected this weekend.
The Warriors have kicked on since that dominant win and sent shockwaves through the competition last week with a commanding victory over the Panthers.
The result pulled Andrew Webster's side within two points of Penrith and the Roosters on the ladder as they look to secure a top-two finish and a home final in the opening week of the post-season.
Brisbane are set to miss out on the finals this year but they produced a blistering start to last week's clash with the Dolphins and have the talent across the park to cause the Warriors plenty of problems.
Ezra Mam is in fine attacking form, while Reece Walsh can shift a match in the blink of an eye.

After dispatching the competition leaders with perhaps their best performance of the NRL season, NZ Warriors must now to maintain that form through the remaining four weeks of the regular season and into the playoffs.
Coach Andrew Webster is still reluctant to rate the 28-12 win over Penrith Panthers ahead of the drought-breaking win over Melbourne Storm in April, even though the Storm have since fallen out of post-season contention.
"I have so much respect for both clubs and what they've done for such a long time now," he said. "I think the opponent has a part to do with it, both of them.
"I still think, with Melbourne, we had a lot of history and hadn't won, and to be so dominant that night sent a message to ourselves.
"To back it up, heading into the finals, they both hold big moments for this club this year particularly."
Webster has never been one to use the points table as motivation, but if he did, he would see his team are still only third in the standings and still only two points ahead of the chasers for a top-four position.
The key is keeping his players grounded and focused on the task ahead.
"I feel like you need to get the balance between hard work and getting to the start-line feeling good," he said. "We have to have energy to go after the contest, but at the same time, you have to keep working hard to improve.
"You have to pick your days and moments, the days you travel, what you feed them - it's like training a racehorse, but it's all important.
"Keeping them really happy, and making sure there's laughter and we're enjoying ourselves, because it's a long campaign between now and the end of it hopefully."
Here's what you need to know about Warriors v Broncos.
History
The Warriors have 23 of their previous 52 previous meetings with one draw. That deadlock came in 2019 at Suncorp Stadium, when they led 16-6 at halftime, but needed a late penalty by Issac Luke to draw level.
In the last 10 encounters, the Warriors have a 5-4 edge, plus that draw. They won the last meeting 42-12 at 'Magic Round' in May, with wing Dallin Watene-Zelezniak scoring a try double.
Halfback Tanah Boyd lasted about five minutes of that game, before suffering a season-ending knee injury .
The rivals split their 2025 match-up - halfback Luke Metcalf kicked a golden point penalty, when Reece Walsh's kickoff went dead on the full for a 20-18 in April, but suffered a season-ending knee injury at Suncorp Stadium in June, as the Warriors lose 26-12.

The Broncos have the biggest margin in the rivalry, winning their second-ever meeting 44-6, with centre Steve Renouf scoring four tries.
The Warriors' biggest win came in 2013, when wings Glen Fisiiahi and Manu Vatuvei, centre Konrad Hurrell and five-eighth Tommy Leuluai all had try doubles in a 56-18 avalanche.
Form
The Warriors are coming off back-to-back wins against Gold Coast Titans - their biggest margin of the season - and the Panthers - probably their most important.
Last Friday, they never trailled against the Panthers at Mt Smart, leading 18-0 at halftime and holding off a late rally to prevail 28-12. Metcalf celebrated his return to the starting line-up with two tries and 16 points.
After losing four of seven games through May-June-July, they have won four of their last five and, at 14-6, they sit third on the table, now four points behind Sydney Roosters and two behind the Panthers, and two ahead of Cronulla Shark

Wests’ most recent game was the 16-13 loss to Parramatta in Round 22, before their Round 23 bye. It was hardly inspiring football. The Eels completed just 67 per cent, made 19 errors and handed the Tigers repeated opportunities to win, yet Wests still found a way to lose. Adam Doueihi briefly put them ahead with a field goal before Parramatta stole the result late.
The positive is that it was at least competitive. After some truly horrendous defensive performances across the previous month, the Tigers restricted Parramatta to 16 and remained in the game for the full 80 minutes.
The bye may have been exactly what this club needed.
There has been relentless scrutiny around Benji Marshall and the playing group, and the Tigers have looked emotionally exhausted as much as physically poor. Having a weekend where they were not required to play, and, importantly, were not the centre of another match day disaster, could allow them to reset.
The team list contains genuine talent. Bula remains dangerous from fullback, Luai and Doueihi form an experienced halves pairing and Koroisau is still capable of controlling a match from dummy half. Terrell May and Fonua Pole give them power through the middle, with Samuela Fainu, Alex Twal, Sione Fainu and Bunty Afoa adding plenty of size.
The backline has been reshuffled again. NSW Cup leading try scorer Solomone Saukuru is set for his NRL debut in the centres, while Junior Tupou and Sunia Turuva occupy the wings. Heamasi Makasini and Starford To’a are out.
There are absolutely no guarantees. But after seven straight defeats, the Tigers are at least rested and facing the only team around their level in my power ratings.
Dragons Produce Their Grand Final Performance
St George Illawarra’s 24-16 upset of Cronulla was easily their best win of the season. The Dragons entered as huge underdogs against a Sharks side sitting fourth but defended with enormous commitment and found the decisive attacking moments late. Setu Tu scored in the 77th minute to seal the result after Cronulla had briefly levelled the scores at 16-16.
The individual efforts were extraordinary. Gutherson ran for 201 metres from 26 carries and broke seven tackles. Ryan Couchman produced 148 metres and an incredible 67 tackles, while Jacob Liddle played the full 80 minutes and made 56 tackles. Young back-rower Hamish Stewart also impressed with 42 tackles and a spectacular first half try.

Panthers vs Roosters Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 24 2026
August 12 th 2026, 10:46pm , By: Scooby
It is a blockbuster start to Round 24 of the NRL this week and it is a preview of what is ahead in September as the Panthers host the Roosters . Both teams are sitting at the top of the competition ladder and as the stage is set for an exhilarating contest, fans of the game will be tuning in to see how each team performs. Before You Bet is here to add to your enjoyment with a detailed preview of what is ahead in this match, with the aim of finding you a winner or two to add to your enjoyment.
Also, Before You Bet will be providing free previews and betting tips for EVERY game in the 2026 NRL season, so make sure to head over to our NRL Tips regularly to keep up to date with all of our free content.
Panthers vs Roosters Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 24 2026
Wounded Panthers character tested
Ambushed on the road by the Warriors, the Panthers left New Zealand with more than just a 28-12 loss to their name. The injury suffered to Issah Yeo could be catastrophic for their 2026 campaign. Kept scoreless until the 67th minute, the Panthers struggled with just 47% possession and a 75% completion rate. Their opponents continually rattled them with physical defence, and they failed to adjust. Considering who was absent, perhaps the loss wasn’t as strange as it appeared. The fact that they made 8.6m per carry and had 5 line breaks given the circumstances offers promise moving forward.
Class rises when it matters most
Expected to struggle with several key players absent, the Roosters display the mentality and execution you would expect from a team of their standing to score two tries in 15 minutes in a 20-18 come-from-behind victory at home over the Bulldogs. With just a 49% share of possession and a 72% completion rate, they made just 8m per carry and had only 2 line breaks. Momentum was with their opponents, but they took their chances when it mattered. They will need to improve defensively; they allowed 5 line breaks and conceded more PCM’s which are both factors superior teams will punish them for in September.
Stats that matter
- These two sides met in Round 3 where the Panthers were victorious 40-4. This extended the Panthers dominance over the Roosters where they have won 12 of 13 since 2020. The home side has a 59% record at this ground with the Roosters striking at 63%.
- In the past 5 games between these two sides, the average margin of victory is 19.2 points, with 3 games decided by 20 points or more. The average total points is 48.8.
- The Panthers are the superior team on both sides of the ball this season. They score 29ppg in attack and concede just 15ppg defensively. The Roosters are not far behind them; they average 27ppg in attack and allow 19ppg in defence.
A hard road ahead
The strength and depth of the Panthers is set to be further tested as they head into this important fixture. Somehow, with 2 of their starting spine players still absent – Edwards is named in the reserves – they are favourites for this match. Now, with Yeo out, the depth of their forwards will be tested further. The Roosters are fortunate to welcome back Tedesco to their team this week, with a timely rest sure to give him the ability to get his body right for this game. It is puzzling to see how the home side are favourites; momentum is with the visitors and despite a horrendous record against the Panthers, the Rooters appear to have confidence and class going into this encounter.
With the Minor Premiership on the line, we are likely to see the best each team has to offer. As good as the Roosters have been recently, there are still some lingering questions about their ability to execute consistently.
